analysis.title: The Conference Board Leading Economic Index Unexpectedly Fell in October
key_insights: The Conference Board Leading Economic Index (LEI) fell 0.3% in October to 99.3 (2016=100) after a flat September reading. Consensus expected an unchanged reading.
The LEI has declined year-on-year for 52 consecutive months. The year-ago growth rate was unchanged at -0.5%.
The LEI's six-month growth rate slipped to 0.1% between April and October, down from 0.6% over the previous six months. PNC reads the positive 0.1% as pointing to continued growth at a slower pace.

Four of the ten LEI components decreased, led by private housing building permits (-0.23%) and average consumer expectations for business conditions (-0.22%). Building permits were at their weakest level since May 2020.

Average weekly manufacturing hours and manufacturers' new orders for nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft fell more modestly. The largest increases came from the interest rate spread (10-year Treasury minus fed funds rate, +0.14%) and the Leading Credit Index (+0.07%).

The Coincident Economic Index (CEI) was unchanged in October after a 0.1% increase in September. Its six-month growth rate improved to 0.7% from 0.4% over the prior six months. All CEI components except industrial production contributed positively.
The Lagging Economic Index was unchanged in October. Its six-month growth rate eased to 0.7% from 0.8%.

PNC's outlook has growth supported by continued AI-related spending and resilient consumer spending. PNC expects the FOMC to raise the fed funds rate by 25 basis points in December and by another 25 basis points in March 2027, to a range of 4.25% to 4.50%, with inflation still well above the Fed's 2% objective.
